title: Remove a Value
statement:
Return a list with **every copy of `value` removed** from `numbers`. The numbers that stay keep their original order.

Do it in a single pass with a **write position**: copy each number you keep to the next free place instead of deleting from the middle of the list.

examples.explanation: All three 2s are removed; the rest keep their order.

hints.nudge: Deleting from the middle of a list shifts everything after it. How can you avoid shifting by building the result at the FRONT of the same list?
hints.pattern: Read pointer and write pointer: read every number; when it is not the value, write it at the write position and advance the write position.
hints.pseudocode:
write = 0
for read in 0..n-1:
  if numbers[read] != value: numbers[write] = numbers[read]; write += 1
return the first `write` numbers
hints.walkthrough: Removing one element at a time from the middle of an array costs O(n) each, so O(n^2) overall. Use two positions instead. `read` visits every number once. `write` marks where the next KEPT number must go. When the number at `read` is not the value, copy it to `write` and move `write` on; when it is the value, skip it (write stays). Since write never gets ahead of read, you never overwrite a number you still need. At the end the first `write` numbers are exactly the kept ones in the original order. O(n) time and O(1) extra memory (apart from the answer).
